children: T-Mobile US stock continued to rise on Thursday after a report that activist investor Elliott Investment Management is pushing Deutsche Telekom to abandon a potential merger with T-Mobile US.

Elliott has built a sizable stake in Deutsche Telekom and wants the German telecom company to pursue other ways of boosting shareholder value, such as larger share buybacks, according to a Bloomberg report on Wednesday citing people familiar with the matter. That report pushed T-Mobile stock up about 3%.
The shares were rising another 0.5% on Thursday. Deutsche Telekom shares were up more than 1%.

Deutsche Telekom already owns a little more than half of T-Mobile. The company has been considering a deal that would put both Deutsche Telekom and T-Mobile under a new parent company owned by their existing shareholders. If completed, it would be the largest public-company merger ever.
The exact size of Elliott's Deutsche Telekom stake isn't known.
Both stocks have struggled over the past 12 months. Deutsche Telekom shares are down about 8%, while T-Mobile has fallen nearly 26%.

Representatives from Elliott and T-Mobile US weren't immediately available to comment. Deutsche Telekom said it does not comment on whether, and if so, to what extent, individuals or companies hold stakes in Deutsche Telekom.
